sentences.text: Appearance:
Mr. Brijendra Kumar Vaishya - Advocate for the appell  Miss Geeta Yadav- G.A. for State.
Mr. Ashok Kumar Shah, learned counsel for the respond  ORDER

This criminal appeal has been filed under Section 14-A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989.

Appellant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.714/2024 registered at Police Station Waidhan, District Singrauli, for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 506 of IPC and also Section 3(2)(v) and 3 (1) (w) (i) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
Appellant is in jail since 18.5.2024.
As per the prosecution story, allegations against the present appellant are that he forcibly took away the prosecutrix and committed rape of prosecutrix.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that prosecutrix is aged about 20 years.
Incident occurred on 14.4.2024 and report has been lodged NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:46214 2 CRA-9467-2024 on 15.04.2024, for which no explanation has been furnished.
There are no call details on record pertaining to conversation between prosecutrix and fiance 'B', would be husband of prosecutrix.
Further, there is no statement of prosecutrix's fiance 'B", would be husband of prosecutrix, on record.

It is also urged that appellant and prosecutrix were in contact with each Ajaj Beg vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45616060/
1 other since February, 2023.

sentences.text: Charge sheet has been filed.
He further submits that trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the appellant be released on bail pending the trial.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail.
Learned counsel for the objector submits that appellant informed 'B', would be husband of the prosecutrix.
Therefore, prosecutrix's marriage got breakdown.
She did not lodge the report, as it would have affected his marriage.
On above grounds, it has been prayed that the application be dismissed.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and in the absence of evidence available on record with respect to conversation between prosecutrix and her fiance 'B', would be husband, I am inclined to release the appellant on bail.
Consequently, this appeal stands allowed.

It is directed that appellant-Ajaj Beg be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a c o n d i t i o n t h a t h e s h a l l r e m a i n p r e s e n t b e f o r e t h e N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2024:MPHC-JBP:46214 3 CRA-9467-2024 concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
